{
  "narrative_text": "The differential metabolome is dominated by androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism, producing one of the strongest cross-paradigm enrichment signals in this dataset. Three independent tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-direct network analysis) converge on the steroid hormone axis: KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) achieves an FDR of 6.0×10⁻¹⁸ in ORA, while the mummichog empirical-compound network independently ranks C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis first with p=0.00042 and a remarkable 100% compound-overlap (15 of 15 pathway metabolites matched). Six driver steroids are shared across both paradigms: testosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, estradiol, estrone, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). RaMP additionally maps these same six compounds to the SMPDB Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068), the 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency context (SMPDB:SMP00356), and the Reactome Estrogen/Androgen biosynthesis modules, all with FDR < 5×10⁻¹². The four non-steroid metabolites (coumarin, N-acetylgalactosamine, xanthine, beta-mercaptoethanol) contribute to peripheral hits including xenobiotics metabolism (coumarin), sialic acid/N-glycan pathways (N-acetylgalactosamine), and purine metabolism (xanthine), but these are secondary to the overwhelming steroid signal. The biological interpretation is that the treatment perturbation strongly dysregulates the C21-steroidogenesis axis at multiple enzymatic steps, affecting both the androgen arm (DHEA → androstenedione → testosterone → DHT) and the aromatase-converted estrogen arm (androstenedione → estrone → estradiol), consistent with an aromatase or HSD17B-axis perturbation.",

Six driver steroids are shared across both paradigms: testosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, estradiol, estrone, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). RaMP additionally maps these same six compounds to the SMPDB Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068), the 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency context (SMPDB:SMP00356), and the Reactome Estrogen/Androgen biosynthesis modules, all with FDR < 5×10⁻¹². The four non-steroid metabolites (coumarin, N-acetylgalactosamine, xanthine, beta-mercaptoethanol) contribute to peripheral hits including xenobiotics metabolism (coumarin), sialic acid/N-glycan pathways (N-acetylgalactosamine), and purine metabolism (xanthine), but these are secondary to the overwhelming steroid signal. The six driver steroids — dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), androstenedione (C00280), testosterone (C00535), dihydrotestosterone (C03917), estrone (C00468), and 17β-estradiol (C00951) — are verified members of this pathway (metabolites_hit = 6, fold enrichment = 1501).
